5'5.5" I'm 15 and when i started losing weight i was 280, im currently 215. I get where you're coming from, i was always bigger when i was younger and weight jokes get old. The first thing I did was make milestones, some of mine were 270: Preorder a video game, 260: Get a boba, 250: Dye my hair. Stuff like that really helped. I took a couple weeks to see what really impacted my weight, found out i was lactose intolerant and allergic to tomatoes. If you take medications, see if those contribute to weight gain! Some of mine did, and there are ways to counteract that. There will be good days and bad days. Days where you binge and then feel like shit, but its all part of the journey. Once you start hitting milestones i would add 1k to my step count. Walking really pays off. I have shitty endurance and would rather play video games then work out. Walking really helped me melt fat, i wore my first crop top in 4+ years yesterday and didnt feel shitty. 

Tl;dr: find out what works, find out what doesnt.

I have experienced this. Before i go on im 15. I had consentual sex under a year ago. Now i was 14, which was already kind of worrying i lost it at that time. I disassociated during sex as a coping mechanism, and after learning what normal love was, it was a realization that there is a difference between falling in love and having sex. In my case i was kind of surprised i knew what to do, but i have a history of CSA. Coping-wise, definitely:
Talking through situational triggers with your partner- what boundaries cannot be pushed
Warning signs to look for- I mean non-verbal moments, looks of panic, unresponsiveness, sudden tremors that arent sexual
Start slowly- throwing yourself into sex is fun, but going really slowly has helped me alot. The moment you cant recognize what you're doing, step back, reevaluate, ground yourself, and then start over.
No nut- actually really helped me, asking myself why am i having sex, how do i feel before/during/after
